newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary to allow 150,000 tonnes barley export.
newsitem.headline: Hungary to allow 150,000 tonnes barley export.

text.p: Hungary's Agriculture Ministry said on Monday it would grant barley export licences for a maximum 150,000 tonnes from the 1996/97 crop.
Each applicant can submit bids for a maximum 20,000 tonnes for export and if total applications exceed 150,000 tonnes, licences will be reduced proportionally, the ministry said in a statement.
Exporters will have to deposit 1,500 forints per tonne and the sum will only be reimbursed if they deliver at least 80 percent of the licensed amount, it added.
Applications can be submitted from July 1 to September 30 and licenses are valid until October 31.
The ministry forecast a 1.223 million tonnes barley crop for 1996/97, of which 626,000 tonnes were spring and 597,000 tonnes were autumn-sown.
Last year Hungary's barley crop was 930,000 tonnes of which 477,000 were spring and 453,000 tonnes were autumn, Central Statistical Office figures showed.
